author: swain
title: Cut Loki reads from alert rules
body:
Alert rules are about 75% of what we read from Loki, roughly 750 GB/day over the last week. That has the account sitting at about 80% of the included query allowance, and it is the reason the "Loki query budget nearly spent" alert is firing. Going over the allowance gets queries rejected with HTTP 429, and since `execErrState` is `Alerting`, that fires every log rule at once, as it did on 2026-09-28.

Three things were inflating the reads.

Every log rule ran as a range query. The model JSON never said `queryType: "instant"`, the same key that blinded the door-knocking recording rule on 2026-09-29, so Loki read each rule's fetch window on top of its range vector, for the one value `reduce: last` keeps. Measured against prod today, that is 2.4x the bytes of the instant query on a 10-minute rule and 3x on an hour. It also meant rules looked back further than their messages said: Peerly looked back 25 minutes while claiming 10.

Rules that fire on any single log line carried 5-minute to 1-hour windows, and the width was there to hold the alert open, not to find the line. They now read one minute, every minute, with a 30-second offset for ingestion lag, and use `keepFiringFor` to keep one incident as one page. Detection stays at a minute for all of them. P2P paid-not-scheduled, robocall and SMS get faster: they were evaluated every 5 minutes.

Dev provisioned the full rule set, paged nobody (non-prod routes to `nowhere`), and still read 211 GB/day. Dev now provisions no alerting at all.

Under the corrected cost model the rule set goes from about 340 days of the gp-api prod stream per day, per environment, to 92 in prod only. I expect alert reads to fall from ~860 GB/day to roughly 200-250. The ratio rules also drop their duplicate floor leg, so they read their window twice rather than three times. Ingest and ad-hoc queries are deliberately untouched.

`global-alerts.test.ts` used fetch window ÷ interval as each rule's cost, which undercounted by more than half. It now sums the range vectors, and new tests pin the instant key, keep each rule's displayed window equal to what it reads, and fail any rule whose window leaves a gap between evaluations.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes detection timing, firing duration (`keepFiringFor`), and LogQL evaluation for all prod log alerts; misconfiguration could miss events or page differently until deploy stabilizes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Cuts Grafana Loki spend by changing how log alert rules query and how rare-event rules stay open, and by stopping dev from provisioning rules that never page.
> 
> **Instant LogQL queries** — `grafana.ts` now sets `queryType: "instant"` in each log rule’s model JSON (and default datasource config), so evaluations read only the range vectors in `expr` instead of fetch window + vector under range mode. `grafana.test.ts` asserts every log rule is instant.
> 
> **Event rules** — Single-line alerts move to `[1m]` vectors, 60s evaluation, 30s `timeRangeOffsetSeconds`, `for: 0m`, and new optional **`keepFiringFor`** (replacing multi-minute/hour windows that only kept incidents open). Messages and `timeRangeSeconds` align with what is actually read.
> 
> **Ratio rules** — `public-campaigns` and `public-person-profiles` error-ratio expressions apply the volume floor on the denominator in one leg (two window reads per eval instead of three).
> 
> **Provisioning scope** — Non-prod deploys skip alert folders, rules, and recording-rule consumers; only prod provisions alerting. Docs reflect prod-only alerting and updated query-cost math.
> 
> **Budget tests** — `rereadFactor` sums range-vector seconds ÷ interval; total cap lowered (130 → 120); new checks that displayed window equals widest vector and window ≥ interval.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 080676f4f09f73acf86ea0cb031602e2327f5929. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
